key_insight: A small, identifiable subset of neurons in LLMs strongly predicts whether a reasoning step will be correct, and steering those neurons' activations at test time (via AdaRAS) reliably improves reasoning without expensive retraining or heavy sampling.
problem_solved: Improves LLM reasoning reliability at inference time while avoiding costly post-training adjustments or computationally expensive sampling strategies.
method: Identify reasoning-critical neurons by measuring predictive correlations between neuron activations and reasoning correctness across examples.

Learn a lightweight, adaptive test-time controller (AdaRAS) that steers those neurons' activations—e.g., rescaling, replacing, or transferring activation patterns—conditioned on confidence/predicted error.
Apply activation transfer/steering across prompts or models as a minimal, deployable intervention to correct likely failure modes without full fine-tuning.
impact: Enables more reliable LLM reasoning with low compute overhead and easy test-time integration, giving practitioners a practical, interpretable tool to reduce failures and cut down on expensive sampling or retraining.
visual_elements: Heatmap over model layers/tokens highlighting the small subset of reasoning-critical neurons
Before vs. after bar chart or line plot showing improvement in reasoning accuracy or failure rates with AdaRAS
Schematic of inference-flow: input → model → activation probe → AdaRAS controller → steered activations → output
Diagram illustrating activation transfer: correct-instance activations used to fix a failing-instance activation pattern
paper_title: Identifying and Transferring Reasoning-Critical Neurons: Improving LLM Inference Reliability via Activation Steering
paper_authors: Fangan Dong, Zuming Yan, Xuri Ge, Zhiwei Xu, Mengqi Zhang
